articles.title: The Sleeping Pill Your Doctor Prescribed May Be Wrecking Your Morning Drive. A World-First Trial Just Proved It.
articles.excerpt: Low-dose quetiapine — increasingly prescribed off-label for insomnia — impaired next-day driving and slowed reaction times. One in four people did not even notice.
articles.image_caption: Seroquel (quetiapine) 25mg tablets, increasingly prescribed off-label for insomnia despite new safety concerns

sources.label: Annals of the American Thoracic Society

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Personalised Cancer Vaccine Just Kept Melanoma Away for Five Years. The Technology Behind It Could Change Everything.
articles.excerpt: Moderna and Merck's mRNA vaccine, custom-built from each patient's tumour DNA, cut the risk of recurrence by 49 per cent in the longest follow-up of any individualized cancer treatment ever tested.
articles.image_caption: Moderna headquarters, developer of the personalized mRNA cancer vaccine
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Asian Americans Use Anxiety Medication at Half the Rate of White Americans. The Reasons Go Deeper Than Stigma.
articles.excerpt: A national study of 29,000 adults found that Asian Americans with diagnosed anxiety disorders are 45 per cent less likely to take medication than their white peers. For the South Asian diaspora, the data confirms a crisis hiding in plain sight.
articles.image_caption: Mental health treatment gaps persist across Asian American communities
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Eating Within a Six-Hour Window Rewired the Gut in Eight Weeks. Your Dadi's Fasting Rules Were Doing the Same Thing.
articles.excerpt: A landmark trial found that time-restricted eating reshaped gut bacteria, lowered body fat, and improved heart-health markers. For South Asians with the highest metabolic risk in America, the science is catching up with tradition.
articles.image_caption: A traditional Indian thali with fermented foods that support the gut microbiome
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Harvard Says Meditation Rewires Your Brain in Two Minutes. Your Grandmother Said It First.
articles.excerpt: A new EEG study finds breath-watching meditation triggers measurable brain changes almost immediately — and the effects peak at seven minutes. The Indian diaspora's ancestral practice now has hard neuroscience behind it.
articles.image_caption: Illustration of brain regions affected by mindfulness meditation practice
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi's Personal Yoga Guru Will Lead Times Square on June 21. Here Is What NRIs Need to Know.
articles.excerpt: International Yoga Day 2026 is coming to the Lincoln Memorial and Times Square, with events designed around the health risks that hit South Asians hardest.
articles.image_caption: Hundreds of practitioners performing yoga together during International Day of Yoga celebrations
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A New Insulin Pump Just Managed Diabetes Without Any Human Input. South Asians Should Be Watching.
articles.excerpt: Pivotal trial data from ADA 2026 shows the Omnipod 6 system delivers 50 per cent more automated insulin, and a fully closed-loop prototype eliminates carb counting entirely.
articles.image_caption: A continuous glucose monitor sensor worn on the arm, the kind of wearable technology driving automated insulin delivery
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Wegovy Now Helps Sleep Apnoea and Asthma, Not Just Weight Loss. South Asians Should Be Paying Attention.
articles.excerpt: New data from four major trials presented at ADA 2026 show semaglutide improves obstructive sleep apnoea, reduces asthma flare-ups, lowers blood pressure, and protects the liver — benefits that go well beyond the number on the scale.
articles.image_caption: A semaglutide injection pen used for weight management and cardiometabolic health
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Targeting 120 Instead of 140 Cut Cardiovascular Deaths by 39 Per Cent. Most South Asians Are Still Aiming Too High.
articles.excerpt: The ESPRIT trial tracked 11,255 high-risk adults for three years and found that aggressive blood pressure lowering dramatically reduced heart attacks, strokes, and death — findings that carry outsized relevance for a community where one in three adults has hypertension.
articles.image_caption: A clinician measuring blood pressure — the ESPRIT trial suggests lower targets save more lives
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: DKA Hospitalisations Have Jumped 24 Per Cent in Seven Years. Most Diabetics Had Never Heard of It.
articles.excerpt: New data presented at ADA 2026 reveals diabetic ketoacidosis is driving nearly 60 per cent of all paediatric diabetes hospitalisations in the United States. The condition is now increasingly striking Type 2 patients — the demographic South Asians dominate globally.
articles.image_caption: A continuous glucose monitor displays real-time blood sugar readings — but current devices do not measure ketones
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A South Asian Man Reversed His Diabetes for Ten Years Without Medication. His Diet Is One His Grandmother Would Recognise.
articles.excerpt: A landmark study published in Frontiers in Nutrition documents the first case of decade-long, drug-free Type 2 diabetes remission in a normal-weight Indian vegetarian male. The secret was not a Western fad diet but a culturally adapted approach built around dal, paneer, and fermented dosa.
articles.image_caption: A traditional Indian vegetarian thali with dal, vegetables, and rice — the foundation of the culturally adapted diet used in the study
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Remote Work Has Made American Tech Workers Lonelier, Sadder, and More Medicated. A Landmark Study Explains Why.
articles.excerpt: A study of 588,322 workers finds the shift to working from home accounts for a third of America's post-pandemic mental health decline. Indian tech professionals are squarely in the blast zone.
articles.image_caption: A remote worker at home — a landmark study links isolation to declining mental health in tech (Wikimedia Commons)

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: South Asians in America Hit Peak Heart Risk at 45 Despite Eating Better and Drinking Less Than Everyone Else.
articles.excerpt: A decade-long study of 2,700 adults found that by age 45, South Asians had the highest rates of prediabetes and hypertension of any racial group — even though they reported healthier habits. The researchers say screening should start much earlier.
articles.image_caption: A doctor conducts a cardiac screening examination
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Daily Pill Just Doubled Survival for Pancreatic Cancer. Oncologists Wept When They Saw the Data.
articles.excerpt: Daraxonrasib targets the KRAS mutation that drives 90 per cent of pancreatic tumours. In a trial of 500 patients, it cut the risk of death by 60 per cent. The FDA is fast-tracking approval.
articles.image_caption: Cancer research laboratory where targeted therapies are being developed
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Sweeps Five Golds at the World's First Yogasana Championship. The Sport Is Chasing Olympic Recognition.
articles.excerpt: More than 400 athletes from 60 countries competed in Ahmedabad. India's dominance was total from the opening day.
articles.image_caption: International Day of Yoga celebration at University of Patanjali, Haridwar
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ultraprocessed Foods Raise Your Dementia Risk by 58 Per Cent. Harvard Tracked 5,300 People for a Decade.
articles.excerpt: Processed meats are the worst offenders. Whole foods cut risk by 41 per cent. For South Asians abandoning traditional diets, the numbers are a warning.
articles.image_caption: Ultraprocessed packaged foods increasingly dominate grocery aisles — and diaspora kitchen shelves
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ninety Minutes of Weight Training a Week Lowers Your Risk of Dying by 13 Per Cent. The Study Tracked 147,000 People for 30 Years.
articles.excerpt: The largest-ever study on strength training and longevity found a sweet spot of 90 to 120 minutes a week — with the biggest surprise being a 27 per cent drop in neurological disease deaths.
articles.image_caption: A person performing dumbbell strength training exercises at a gym
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A British-Made Pill Just Shrank Tumours Across Six Cancer Types. Every Patient Had Run Out of Options.
articles.excerpt: The Oxford-developed drug GRWD5769 strips away cancer's 'invisibility cloak,' allowing immunotherapy to work in patients where it had failed. The ASCO results are early but remarkable.
articles.image_caption: Cancer researchers at a clinical trial laboratory studying immunotherapy treatments
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The First Major Trial of Probiotics for Cancer Treatment Just Began. The Science Behind It Is Rooted in Your Gut.
articles.excerpt: Nearly 700 patients will test whether a common Japanese probiotic can boost immunotherapy. South Asians, whose traditional diets are rich in fermented foods, have reason to watch closely.
articles.image_caption: A scientist examines bacterial cultures in a research laboratory
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Obesity Drugs Just Stole the Show at ADA 2026. South Asians Should Pay Close Attention.
articles.excerpt: Roche's injection hit 22.7 per cent weight loss in 48 weeks. An oral pill showed no liver damage. A third drug barely caused nausea. The obesity treatment landscape is about to change.
articles.image_caption: A researcher works in a pharmaceutical laboratory developing new drug treatments
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: GLP-1 Weight-Loss Drugs May Cut Cancer Risk by Up to 70 Per Cent. Five ASCO Studies Explain Why South Asians Should Pay Attention.
articles.excerpt: Pancreatic, lung, breast and blood cancers all showed significant reductions among GLP-1 users in studies covering nearly 900,000 patients presented this week
articles.image_caption: A GLP-1 receptor agonist injection pen used for weight management and diabetes treatment
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The AHA Just Said Exercise Works Even When the Scale Does Not Move. South Asians Need to Hear This.
articles.excerpt: A new scientific statement in Circulation documents that physical activity improves blood pressure, insulin resistance and visceral fat independently of weight loss
articles.image_caption: Regular physical activity improves cardiovascular health even without significant weight loss
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India’s Heatwave Has Killed 56 People and Caused 25,000 Cases of Suspected Heatstroke Since March. If You Are Visiting This Summer, Read This.
articles.excerpt: Thirty-four people died in a single district in Uttar Pradesh in two days — all over 60 with preexisting conditions. Temperatures have breached 42 degrees Celsius across northern India while power outages leave families without fans or running water.
articles.image_caption: Scorching temperatures across India have caused 25,000 suspected heatstroke cases since March
articles.nri_angle: The diaspora summer travel season — June through August, aligned with American and British school holidays — coincides directly with India’s most dangerous heat period. NRIs travelling with elderly parents or young children face specific medical risks.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Unsafe Food Kills 1.5 Million People a Year. South-East Asia and Africa Bear Three Quarters of the Burden.
articles.excerpt: A WHO report covering 194 countries finds that chemical contamination from arsenic and lead now causes 73 per cent of foodborne deaths, children under five face triple the risk, and the global productivity cost exceeds 300 billion dollars annually. The diaspora implications are personal.
articles.image_caption: Street food vendors prepare meals — unsafe food causes 866 million illnesses a year globally
articles.nri_angle: NRIs travelling to India face direct exposure to foodborne risks that disproportionately affect South-East Asia, while families importing traditional foods should be aware of arsenic in rice and lead contamination in spices.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: One in Three World Cup Matches Faces Dangerous Heat. FIFA Just Banned Fans From Bringing Water Bottles.
articles.excerpt: With the tournament kicking off on June 11 across 16 North American cities, an NPR analysis finds 39 matches at high risk for heat illness — and diaspora fans attending in Houston, Dallas, and Miami face the worst conditions.
articles.image_caption: Fans watch a soccer match under sunny skies at an outdoor stadium
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Swapping 100 Grams of Conventional Produce for Organic Each Day Cuts Breast Cancer Risk by 10 Per Cent. The Data Is Getting Hard to Ignore.
articles.excerpt: A seven-year French study of 31,000 women finds that even modest shifts toward organic fruits and vegetables significantly reduce postmenopausal breast cancer risk — with implications for South Asian families navigating pesticide-heavy food systems on two continents.
articles.image_caption: Fresh vegetables and fruits displayed at a local market
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: One in Seven People Now Uses an AI Chatbot Instead of Seeing a Doctor. The Risks Are Not What You Expect.
articles.excerpt: A major UK study finds 15 per cent of the public has replaced GP visits with AI, while a separate trial shows chatbots matching physicians on diagnosis. For a diaspora facing three-month specialist waits, the implications are personal.
articles.image_caption: Fifteen per cent of the British public has used AI chatbots instead of contacting a GP for health concerns
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sleeping Less Than Six Hours a Night Raises Your Osteoarthritis Risk by Up to 40 Per Cent. Night-Shift Workers Face Even Worse Odds.
articles.excerpt: A half-million-person WashU study links short sleep and disrupted circadian rhythms to accelerated joint damage, with implications for every South Asian working late shifts abroad.
articles.image_caption: Participants who slept fewer than six hours a night showed significantly higher risk of joint disease in the UK Biobank study
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Your Child's Brain Is Writing Its Own Code Right Now. Screens Are the Dominant Input.
articles.excerpt: A federal advisory classifies youth screen time as a public health crisis. A new neuroscience framework explains why the damage may be permanent. South Asian parents face an especially sharp dilemma.
articles.image_caption: A young boy illuminated by smartphone screen light at night
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Your Brain Starts Changing Within Two Minutes of Meditation. By Seven Minutes, It Peaks.
articles.excerpt: A study from India's NIMHANS, using the Isha Yoga breath-watching tradition, shows measurable neural shifts happen faster than anyone assumed. For time-starved diaspora professionals, the science says even brief practice works.
articles.image_caption: A person practicing breath-focused meditation outdoors at sunset
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
